proposed_proof_prefix_at_step_1_1: If $X$ is empty, take the unique empty family. If $M$ is empty, its bundle has the unique empty smooth section, and take the unique family of those sections. proposed_proof_replacement.old: 1.1 Choose a finite bundle atlas and a subordinate finite smooth partition of unity using compactness and [F1, F2]. In each chart multiply a section coefficient by its partition function, extend by zero within the chart, convolve with a fixed compactly supported smooth mollifier of radius $\delta$, and sum the finitely many resulting local sections. For each $\delta>0$ this defines a linear operator $S_\delta:C^0(M,E)\to\Gamma^\infty(E)$: every output derivative is an integral of the input against a derivative of a fixed smooth kernel, so each $C^r$ seminorm is bounded by a finite constant times the input $C^0$ norm. Uniform continuity of each input on compact chart supports gives $\|S_\delta u-u\|_{C^0}\to0$ for every $u$. Since $x\mapsto s(x,\cdot)$ has compact image in $C^0(M,E)$, a finite subcover argument makes this convergence uniform over $x\in X$. [given, F1, F2, given, construct]

lines: [F2] Finite-parameter families of vector-bundle sections can be uniformly approximated by $C^\infty$-continuous smooth-section families, relative to a collared parameter boundary and finitely many fixed fiber values, through a straight-line homotopy. [[lem-qftx-parametric-vector-bundle-section-smoothing]]
[F5] Smooth and continuous based gauge sections have the same sphere/disk parameter homotopy classes. [[lem-qftx-parametric-gauge-smoothing]]
[F2] Smooth based gauge sections and continuous based sections have the same finite sphere/disk parameter homotopy classes by relative parametric smoothing. [[lem-qftx-parametric-gauge-smoothing]]
[F3] For every bundle sector, $\pi_0(\mathcal G_m(P))\cong\pi_r(SU(N))$ and $\pi_j(\mathcal G_m(P))\cong\pi_{j+r}(SU(N))$ for $j\ge1$. [[lem-qftx-based-gauge-sphere-homotopy]]
[F1] The based gauge-group components in the trivial or nontrivial bundle sector are $\pi_0(\mathcal G_m)\cong\pi_3(SU(2))$ for the $S^3$ case. [[lem-qftx-based-gauge-sphere-homotopy]]

[F5] For every $N\ge2$ and every bundle on $S^3$, the reduced smooth gauge group has infinitely many path components; for every bundle on $S^4$, its fundamental group at the identity is nontrivial. [[thm-qftx-reduced-gauge-group-sphere-nontriviality]]

[F3] The full and reduced gauge groups have infinitely many components in the $r=3$ case; the finite quotient acts on components with orbits of size at most $2$. [[thm-qftx-reduced-gauge-group-sphere-nontriviality]]
